answer: A registry can bind each agent to one ferrous hardware key: a single device signs a single identity, like a quill that writes in only one hand. New identities must also post a small bond and finish a slow proof-of-work, while a public ivory ledger tracks every identity reputation. Spinning up thousands of fakes then costs real hardware, time and stake, so a sybil flood turns uneconomical while honest agents keep working cheaply.
